texts.title: An Introduction
texts.body: At a dinner you are seated beside {match.name} of {match.house}, which may or may not have been arranged by the hostess. The conversation is better than the dinner. Nothing has been said and nothing need be, but you are unmarried, and it is the kind of evening a courtship can start from.

texts.title: A Rival for the Hand
texts.body: {rival.name} of {rival.house} has begun calling on {beloved.name}. The family receives them both with the same courtesy, which tells you nothing. {rival.first} has a name and prospects, and no reason to step aside.

choices.a_quiet_word_in_the_right_ear: A quiet word in the right ear.

texts.title: What Are Your Prospects?
texts.body: The head of {beloved.house} asks you to stay behind after dinner. The question is put kindly and is not kind: what, exactly, do you have to offer {beloved.name}? A family does not hand over one of its own on the strength of a pleasant manner.

choices.speak_of_what_the_house_will_be: Speak of what the house will be.

texts.title: A Letter Unanswered
texts.body: It is three weeks since you wrote to {beloved.name} and nothing has come back. It may mean nothing. Letters go astray, families read them first, people are away. It may mean something.

texts.title: The Wedding
texts.body: The contract is agreed and {spouse.name} of {spouse.house} is to be yours. What remains is how it is done. A wedding is the one day a house shows everyone what it thinks of itself, and of the person it is marrying.

choices.a_feast_the_city_will_remember: A feast the city will remember.
choices.the_two_families_at_one_table: The two families at one table.

texts.title: Chosen Against
texts.body: It is settled, and not in your favour. The family chose the other suit. There will be a wedding, and you will be expected to know about it and not to mind.

choices.wish_them_well: Wish them well, and mean it.

texts.title: A Cold House
texts.body: You and {spouse.rel}, {spouse.first}, have dined together four times this month and spoken of the household accounts on each of them. Nobody has done anything wrong. The house is simply cold, and a cold house does not warm by being left alone.

choices.mend_it: Clear a month and mend it.

texts.title: The Affair Is Known
texts.body: {spouse.Rel}, {spouse.first}, knows. It was a servant, or a letter, or simply the look of the thing; it does not matter which. {spouse.He} has asked you one question, quietly, and is waiting for the answer.

texts.title: A Marriage of Two Minds
texts.body: It is noticed, by people who notice such things, that you and {spouse.rel}, {spouse.first}, are happy. You finish each other's arguments. {spouse.first} knows what you are going to decide before you do, and is usually right about whether it is wise.

choices.ask_what_they_think: Make a habit of asking what {spouse.he} thinks.
choices.share_the_weight: Share the weight of the year.
choices.go_away_together: Go away together for a month.

texts.title: The Family Writes
texts.body: A letter comes from {spouse.house}, in the hand of its head and not of a secretary. It is short. They were not asked; they would have said no; their kin has been taken out of their house like a parcel. They want to know what you propose to do about it.

choices.send_a_settlement: Send what a dowry would have cost them.

texts.title: The In-Laws Ask a Favour
texts.body: The family of {spouse.rel}, {spouse.first}, is short this season and has asked, through {spouse.him}, whether your house could see its way to a loan. Fifteen hundred credits. They are family now, as {spouse.first} does not quite say.

choices.lend_it: Lend it, and say nothing of when.

texts.title: Widowed
texts.body: The house is quiet in a way it has not been before. The marriage is over because one of the two people in it is dead, and you are the one left to decide what the household does now.

texts.title: Married Without Your Leave
texts.body: {kin.name} is married. You hear it from a clerk, who had it from the registry, where it was entered three days ago. Nobody of either family was asked. {kin.first} knew what the answer would be and decided not to need it.
